answer: Each identity seals a proof: walk 4096 sequential cache lines across pseudo-random RAM offsets, each step dependent on prior line's contents, then hash-seal the terminal state under a nonce. Verifier replays the walk; a forged identity must physically hold the same multi-GB trace, so the summit of viable sockpuppets stays low while honest agents climb cheaply. One mismatch voids the seal, like a zephyr erasing tracks on a glacier. Re-deriving 10,000 identities costs roughly $4,800 in RAM-hours per epoch, making farms uneconomic.
